transcript: If you're in New York and in the market for some feel-good queer art this Pride Month, Rob Madge is presenting their solo show My Son's a Queer (But What Can You Do?) at New York City Center this weekend only. I was at the first performance last night, and it was a tight 70 minutes of laughter, music, home videos, and shameless joy. I feel like there's so much queer art at this point that focuses on the trauma, the struggles, and overcoming them, but it's equally as moving to spotlight radical acceptance and self-assurance. In that sense, I thought this piece was really original and a pleasant surprise. Rob Madge really is a star, and you'll see in the show that they always have been. This absolutely has my recommendation, and if you're under 40 years old, there are $28 tickets available through New York City Center’s Access Club program. With that, another program for my collection.
